items.title: Over a base carrying an ample invertible sheaf, projective morphisms are H-projective and quasi-projective ones are H-quasi-projective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that over a base admitting an ample invertible sheaf, every projective morphism is H-projective and every quasi-projective morphism is H-quasi-projective (statement lines 10847-10854). The counted proof is a short reduction chain: the ample hypothesis makes the base quasi-compact and separated, which gives the second assertion from the first; by the definition of projective morphisms it suffices to treat projective bundles of finite type modules, and those are handled by a closed immersion into a projective space over the base once the module is globally generated by finitely many sections, the general case being reduced to that by twisting the module with a high power of an ample sheaf, which leaves the projective bundle unchanged (proof lines 10856-10882). It is H2: the reductions and the construction are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard ampleness, projective bundle and twisting statements.
